noInvent.title: Nothing invented
noInvent.text: Every rewritten line is linked to a line of your original resume. A new number or degree is blocked until you approve it.

ats.title: ATS-readable
ats.text: One column, standard headings, selectable text: recruiting software reads all of it.

score.title: A score you can explain
score.text: The score is calculated from evidence found in your resume, not guessed. You see what counts.

privacy.title: Your resume isn't kept
privacy.text: Your file is read, analyzed then forgotten: it is never saved. The site and database are hosted in Paris.

honesty.title: What's missing stays visible, never added
honesty.text: If the job asks for a skill you don't have, CV Woo tells you plainly. It doesn't write it into your resume for you.
honesty.item1: Skills you have, with the line from your resume that proves it
honesty.item2: Skills not demonstrated, to highlight better
honesty.item3: Missing skills, listed separately to help you grow

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Yes, during the beta: 1 free tailoring without an account, then 5 a month with a free account. The ATS checker is free with no sign-up. PDF and Word downloads are unlimited.
faq.a2: No. The model is forbidden from adding information, and an automatic check flags any number, date, degree or employer that isn't in your original resume.
faq.q3: What happens to my resume and my data?
faq.a3: Your file is never saved on our servers: it’s read in memory, analyzed, then forgotten. To perform the analysis, its text is sent to our artificial intelligence provider (Anthropic). If you create an account, we only keep your email and your number of tailorings this month.
faq.q4: Does the score guarantee an interview?
faq.a4: No. It's an internal estimate of how well you match the job, not an official ATS score.

hero.title: Does your resume get past recruiting robots?
hero.subtitle: Most companies screen applications with software (an ATS). Check in seconds whether it can read your resume, and what to fix.

readable.title: Text readable by robots
readable.fail: No text could be read: your resume is probably an image or a scan. An ATS will see it as empty. Export it to PDF from Word, Google Docs or Canva (as a “standard PDF”).

layout.title: Simple layout
layout.pass: One column, no tables or text boxes: ideal.
layout.warn: Your resume uses {issues}. Many ATS read these out of order or skip them. See below what a robot reads.

icons.title: Special characters
icons.warn: {count} icons or emojis found: an ATS reads them as gibberish. Replace them with text, such as “Phone:”.

images.title: Images and graphics
images.warn: {count} images found. Skill bars, logos or icons as images are invisible to an ATS. A single photo is fine.

email.title: Email address
email.fail: No email address found in the text: the recruiter won't be able to contact you.

contact_header.title: Readable contact details
contact_header.fail: Your contact details are in the Word header or footer: many ATS don't read them. Move them into the body of the resume.

sections.title: Standard section headings
sections.pass: Experience, Education and Skills are easy to identify.
sections.warn: Section not recognized: {missing}. Use standard headings such as “Experience”, “Education”, “Skills”.
sections.fail: Sections not recognized: {missing}. Use standard headings such as “Experience”, “Education”, “Skills”.

length.title: Resume length
length.short: Only {words} words: your resume is very short and probably lacks details about your work.
length.long: {words} words: your resume is long. Aim for 1 to 2 pages.

quantified.title: Measurable results
quantified.warn: Few measurable results ({count}). If true, add numbers: clients, budget managed, % growth…

dates.title: Date format
dates.mixed: Several date formats mixed ({formats}). Pick one, such as “09/2022 – 06/2024”.
dates.none: No dates recognized. ATS use them to calculate your years of experience.

pages.title: Number of pages

pages.warn: 3 pages: that's long, aim for 1 to 2 pages.
pages.fail: {pages} pages: far too long, aim for 1 to 2 pages.
